settings.companion: father - can act as account holder where an adult is required

ageRulesGlossary.standingRestriction: Any under-16/under-18 limit on terraces or late kick-offs.

clubs.name: FC Bayern München

ageRules.note: Requests are made under the user's own membership. Membership contract itself required a guardian signature under 18.
ageRules.standingRestriction: unknown - German youth protection may limit under-16s at events past 22:00. VERIFY.

procedure.home: Requests via tickets.fcbayern.com. Overbooked fixtures go to a members-only lottery, max 2 tickets. Overbooked home games get a Ticketmarket resale option.
procedure.away: ALL Bundesliga away fixtures for the season requested in ONE pre-season window. Once a fixture shows Overbooked the request option disappears. No away resale on the club site - post-draw waiting list only.
procedure.cup: Pokal ties open their own short window after each round's draw. NOT covered by the pre-season window, so still available this season. No member discount in the Pokal.
procedure.europe: Champions League home games requested pre-season as blind matchday slots.

clubs.demandNote: Away request volumes: Dortmund 135,000, Schalke 106,000, Köln 100,000. Least popular away fixture still drew 60,000.
clubs.openQuestion: Are away allocations weighted by prior away attendance, or a pure member lottery? Determines whether low-demand away days are strategy.

clubs.name: VfB Stuttgart

ageRules.accountHolder: self, but membership needs guardian signature under 18
ageRules.note: Under 18 joins the VfB Fritzle- und Jugendclub, not the adult e.V. Under-18 ticket reduction available; bring proof of age, required without being asked.

procedure.membership: Adult passive e.V. EUR 60/yr. Fritzle- und Jugendclub cheaper, exact fee unconfirmed.
procedure.waitingPeriod: Since 1 July 2025, new members of either body can only use the presale right after THREE MONTHS. Other benefits immediate.
procedure.home: Home matches frequently sell out in the member presale. Max 2 tickets. High-demand fixtures use an application lottery - apply within a multi-day window; timing inside it is irrelevant; random allocation after close.
procedure.pricing: Not published; visible only in the purchase flow. Member discount EUR 17 plus a separate under-18 reduction - verify whether they stack. Cheapest is standing.
procedure.warning: REWE Familienblock (75, 76, 81, 82) is restricted to Fritzle- und Jugendclub members and will be offered - but it is seated and standing is discouraged. Wrong block for atmosphere.

clubs.travel: S6 to Stuttgart Hbf, S1 to Neckarpark, approx 40 min. VVS travel normally included in the ticket.

procedure.home: Sold via ksc.de. Ordinary fixtures normally available in general sale. Derby and big-visitor fixtures sell out.
procedure.away: Away end at KSC home games is allocated by the visiting club.

clubs.name: 1. FC Kaiserslautern

procedure.home: Sold via fck.de. Ordinary fixtures usually buyable.
procedure.away: FCK away allocations run through FCK membership. Required if the target is the away end at Karlsruhe.

clubs.travelNote: Approx 3h by train vs 1h55 by car.

clubs.name: Stuttgarter Kickers

ageRules.note: Cash at the gate, no account needed.

procedure.home: Walk-up, approx EUR 12, no membership, no window, no draw. Big fixtures do sell out - the opener v SSV Ulm on 7 Aug 2026 was a full house.

clubs.role: The no-logistics option. The club to simply turn up to.

clubs.name: Politehnica Timișoara

ageRules.idAtGate: Romanian grounds check names against tickets for high-risk fixtures. Carry ID.
ageRules.note: Free entry at Tribuna 2 for under-12s and Academy juniors only. No discount at 15.

procedure.home: Bilete.ro online AND at the stadium on matchday (gates approx 90 min before). Tribuna 1 is smaller and sells out first.
procedure.seasonTicket: Tribuna 1 600 lei, Tribuna 2 350 lei - Liga 2 regular season plus Cupa României home games.

clubs.warning: 5,000 capacity. Do not plan to walk up for a Superliga opponent.
clubs.context: Boyhood club, 8 years in the academy. Newly promoted to Liga 2. At Electrica because Eroii Timișoarei is unfinished; the old Dan Păltinișanu no longer exists.

clubs.name: UTA Arad

ageRules.note: Child discount stops at 13. Children's tickets restricted to Peluza Sud, sector R.

procedure.home: iabilet.ro via uta-arad.ro, opening approx 4 days ahead. Also Fan Shop at the Arena (typically Tue/Thu/Fri 15:00-18:00) and the matchday box office a few hours before kick-off.
procedure.pricing: Tribuna 1 90 lei, Tribuna 2 70 lei, peluze 50 lei.

clubs.context: Built by Baron Neuman in 1946, modelled on Arsenal's old Highbury.

procedure.home: UNVERIFIED. Small Liga 2 club; gate sales near certain. Announcements via Facebook rather than a portal.

ageRules.accountHolder: unknown - VERIFY before the sale window
ageRules.note: Nominative tickets, name must match ID. No name changes for the derby - each ticket bought in the name of the person using it. This makes the account-holder question critical, not cosmetic.

phases: Phase 1 - OPEN TO EVERYONE WORLDWIDE, primo anello rosso/arancio only. The route from abroad.
Phase 2 - season ticket holders, secondo anello blu
Phase 3 - SiamoNoi cardholders, up to 4 tickets
procedure.warning: In 2025 the allocation sold out after phase 2, so the SiamoNoi phase never opened. The free card gates the LAST phase - it is not a shortcut. Phase 1 is the real route.
procedure.note: Secondo anello blu is the Milan away sector, excluded from that season ticket.
procedure.pricing: Third tier approx EUR 70-75; primo rosso centrale up to EUR 230.

clubs.name: AC Milan

ageRules.note: Nominative, no name change for the derby.

procedure.action: Register and obtain the Cuore Rossonero card WELL before the sale - cards have a cutoff days before the phase opens.

clubs.stadiumNote: New stadium targeted Dec 2030; demolition tender Oct 2030-Mar 2031, partial demolition to May 2032. No urgency.

clubs.name: RC Strasbourg Alsace

ageRules.idAtGate: Some French tickets are personalised. Carry ID.

procedure.ordinary: From approx EUR 20 on the official billetterie, opening approx 1 month ahead. Gates 2h30 before.
procedure.bigMatches: 'Prestige' (PSG, Marseille, Monaco) and 'Gala' (historically Lyon, Metz, Saint-Étienne) are NOT sold as single tickets to non-subscribers - only as TWO-MATCH PACKS, max 2 places, approx 1 month before the first of the pair.
procedure.resale: Official resale is the realistic route for sold-out matches. Only abonnés can list; anyone can buy; club sets prices. Opens 3-5 days before, usually WEDNESDAY.
procedure.warning: Club states its billetterie is the only valid channel. Never Viagogo or StubHub.

clubs.caveat: The pack rule is historical policy. The Meinau renovation completes with 2026/27, so allocation may have loosened. Verify.
clubs.bonus: Women's team plays at the Meinau in the Arkema Première Ligue including v PSG. Cheaper, no pack system - closes the women's-football gap.
clubs.travel: Direct train to Strasbourg, tram A to Lycée Couffignal.

clubs.name: Germany (DFB)
clubs.memberStatus: Fan Club Nationalmannschaft member, in own name

ageRules.note: CONTRADICTS the imported document, which claims DFB tickets must go through an adult's account. The user holds the membership himself and already secured the Sept/Oct 2026 tickets. Document is wrong here.

procedure.home: Fan Club presale via the DFB portal. Cheap fan-block tickets exist but go early. Membership also gives exclusive events and fan-tent access at home internationals.
procedure.away: Separate application window per fixture, typically closing weeks ahead.
procedure.autographs: Open training at adidas Home Ground Herzogenaurach - not every camp, free ticketed, approx 4,000 places, gone within an hour. Tournament base camps are the softest target.

clubs.name: UEFA (finals)

ageRules.accountHolder: DISPUTED - the imported document claims applicants must be 18+, which would mean the father applies and the user is named on the ticket. Not independently confirmed. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-PRIORITY THING TO VERIFY, before Feb 2027.

procedure.ballot: Public application at UEFA.com/tickets, approx 5 days, allocated by RANDOM DRAW after close - day one gives no advantage. Free to enter.
procedure.timing: 2026 precedent: general sales opened 16 March, Europa League deadline 11:00 CET 20 March. Document claims February. Alert late Feb, expect mid-March.
procedure.pricing: 2026 finals ran EUR 40-240. Each finalist received approx 12,000.
procedure.warning: Resellers charge many times face value and UEFA voids tickets bought outside official channels.

clubs.realism: The 2026 Europa League final in Istanbul drew 37,324 - it did not sell out. Odds better than for a Champions League final.

bucketList.title: Der Klassiker - Borussia Dortmund v Bayern, away end
bucketList.why: Stated top priority. Hardest single ticket in German football. Marked as a rivalry rather than a true local derby.
bucketList.blockedReason: The 2026/27 away request window closed 27 July 2026 with no request submitted. Away fixtures cannot be resold on the club site.
bucketList.unblockCondition: Enter the 2027/28 window, expected late July 2027. Request EVERY away fixture in one sitting - unsuccessful requests cost nothing.
bucketList.whyAssistant: Germany's top fixture: Bayern's tifo-heavy Südkurve in Munich, and Dortmund's standing Südtribüne in Dortmund.

bucketList.title: Politehnica Timișoara v UTA Arad - Derby-ul Vestului
bucketList.why: Stated as the single most personally invested derby in world football. A six-time champion (UTA) and a two-time cup winner (Politehnica) from neighbouring western cities, both wrecked by insolvency, both with supports far above their current level.
bucketList.blockedReason: Two obstacles. UTA are Superliga, Poli Liga 2 - no league fixture. And although both are in Cupa României Group A, the format gives each club three matches, one per seeding pot, and Poli's pot-one opponent is Rapid.
unblockCondition: Poli promotion - play-off decided approx mid-May 2027, giving two league meetings from 2027/28.
Both reaching the quarter-finals on 3 Mar 2027 AND same-group pairings being permitted - rule unverified.
bucketList.warning: 3 Mar 2027 is a Wednesday in German term time.
bucketList.whyAssistant: West Romania derby (Derbiul Vestului). Arad's Francisc Neuman stadium opened in 2020; Timișoara's large Dan Păltinișanu was demolished in 2025, with a new stadium planned on the same site, and Politehnica play at the Electrica stadium.

bucketList.title: UEFA Europa League final
bucketList.why: First genuine final above national-cup level. Two hours away, inside the Whitsun holidays (18-29 May 2027). The cheapest European final he will ever have access to.
bucketList.practical: Wednesday, 21:00 kick-off ending near 23:00. Overnight or no realistic train home.
bucketList.whyAssistant: One match in May at a rotating venue.

bucketList.title: Frankenderby - 1. FC Nürnberg v Greuther Fürth
bucketList.why: Neighbouring cities, over a century of open contempt, treated by police as one of Germany's highest-risk fixtures regardless of division. Biggest occasion reachable within 300 km.

nextFixture.derivation: Inferred from the mirrored fixture list - matchday 20 is Bielefeld away on 6 Feb 2027. Verify against the DFL schedule.
nextFixture.missed: First leg at the Ronhof, 15 Aug 2026.

bucketList.whyAssistant: Franconia's local derby between two neighbouring cities.

bucketList.title: Karlsruher SC v 1. FC Kaiserslautern
bucketList.why: Closest big derby available. Fills the derby gap and, via the away end, the away-end gap in one trip.

nextFixture.missed: First leg on the Betzenberg, 15 Aug 2026.

bucketList.fallback: Kaiserslautern v Nürnberg on the Betzenberg, 12-14 Mar 2027. Not a derby, but a large travelling support and the Fritz-Walter-Stadion.
bucketList.whyAssistant: Known as the Südwestderby, played at the Wildpark or at the Fritz-Walter-Stadion on the Betzenberg; the grounds are about 65 km apart in a straight line.

bucketList.title: Derby della Madonnina - Inter v Milan
bucketList.why: Two European giants sharing one stadium, both curve building tifos facing each other. New ground, and closer than Turin - the Allianz Stadium is already attended.

fixtures.saleRoute: Cuore Rossonero phase then free sale. Card needed well in advance.
fixtures.note: Page read by the user's chat assistant on 2026-10-11, not opened by Code; it states «sabato 31 ottobre alle 20:45 (Milan-Inter)». SA.json has the same slot.

fixtures.saleRoute: Phase 1, open worldwide, primo anello rosso/arancio.

bucketList.whyAssistant: Played at San Siro, shared by both clubs and owned by them since 2025; it is expected to be demolished in 2031 or 2032 once a replacement stadium is built.

bucketList.title: Revierderby - Schalke 04 v Borussia Dortmund
bucketList.why: Rated the loudest ninety minutes in German football - two mining-town clubs a few kilometres apart with two of the largest terraces in the world. Live again as a league fixture with Schalke promoted.
bucketList.ticketNote: Both ends effectively closed to non-members. Realistically requires a Schalke membership. Treat as a multi-year item.
bucketList.whyAssistant: Ruhr derby between clubs whose grounds are about 28 km apart in a straight line, often called "the mother of all derbies" in the German media.

bucketList.title: DFB-Pokal first round at an amateur host
bucketList.why: A Bundesliga club at a small ground is usually the loudest night of that club's decade. Uniquely German.

trigger.action: Check the AMATEUR club's own ticket page the week after the draw - the host sells, not the visitor.

bucketList.note: Revenue splits 45/45/10 between home club, away club and the DFB. CORRECTION to the imported document, which puts round 1 at 21-24 August 2026: Bayern played Osnabrück on 2 September.

bucketList.title: Liga 2 promotion play-off, decisive round
bucketList.why: If Poli reach it, the promotion that unblocks poli-uta.

trigger.action: Check Bilete.ro once the top six is settled.

bucketList.title: Bundesliga Relegation, second leg
bucketList.why: The most nervous football in Germany.

trigger.action: Participants unknown until the final matchday. Check the morning after the last round.

bucketList.whyAssistant: Two-legged tie between the 16th-placed Bundesliga club and the 3rd-placed 2. Bundesliga club: the aggregate decides, there is no away-goals rule, and extra time and penalties follow if it is level. One top-flight place is at stake. In 2026 the first leg ended 0:0 and Paderborn beat Wolfsburg 2:1 after extra time in the return leg. The DFB page and Wikipedia agree on the format; the play-offs have been two-legged since 2008/09.

bucketList.title: Eternal Derby - Red Star v Partizan
bucketList.why: Rated the best pyrotechnic display in world football, in a stadium where the noise is constant for ninety minutes.
bucketList.deferReason: Stadium safety culture well below German standards. Flagged in the source as an item for 17-18+, with a neutral section and no colours. Not a next-season entry.
bucketList.whyAssistant: The Belgrade "Eternal Derby", among Europe's loudest atmospheres.

bucketList.title: Intercontinental Derby - Galatasaray v Fenerbahçe
bucketList.why: Rated the most intimidating atmosphere in European football. Frequently played with away fans banned.
bucketList.deferReason: Same category as Belgrade. Older item.
bucketList.whyAssistant: One of the loudest derbies anywhere, split between Europe and Asia. Away fans are often banned.

bucketList.title: Old Firm - Celtic v Rangers
bucketList.why: Rated the most tribal fixture in Europe.
bucketList.deferReason: Effectively unavailable to anyone who is not a season-ticket holder at one of the two clubs. A European night at Celtic Park is the achievable version of the same ground.
bucketList.whyAssistant: A unique atmosphere with deep historical baggage. Away allocations vary.

bucketList.title: Derby of the Eternal Enemies - Olympiacos v Panathinaikos
bucketList.why: Working-class Piraeus against establishment Athens. One of the most hostile environments in Europe.
bucketList.relatedNear: PAOK at Toumba - already came close once and missed by finding out late.
bucketList.whyAssistant: Athens' biggest rivalry.

bucketList.title: Eternul derby - FCSB v Dinamo București
bucketList.why: Army club against Interior Ministry club. Both have declined; the hatred has not.
bucketList.ticketNote: ID-named and sells out. Heaviest policing and segregation in Romanian football.
bucketList.alternative: Rapid at Giulești (country rank 3) is the more relaxed first choice and among the loudest atmospheres in the country.
bucketList.whyAssistant: Bucharest's biggest fixture. Venues vary and are unverified.

bucketList.title: Derby du Nord - Lens v Lille
bucketList.why: By common consent the best atmosphere in France. Bollaert is full and singing whatever division Lens are in. Cheap tickets, expensive travel.
bucketList.whyAssistant: Lens's Bollaert-Delelis is among France's most atmospheric stadiums.

bucketList.title: Ostderby - Dynamo Dresden v Hansa Rostock
bucketList.why: Rated arguably the most volatile fixture in Germany. Two former East German champions with two of the hardest supports in the country.
bucketList.practical: 5-6 hours from Stuttgart. Overnight trip, not a day out.
bucketList.whyAssistant: East German rivalry between two large supporter bases, with heavy security around it.

bucketList.title: Prague Derby - Sparta v Slavia
bucketList.why: Central Europe's biggest domestic rivalry, and among the most affordable foreign trips available after Strasbourg and Basel.
bucketList.related: Wiener Derby - Rapid Wien v Austria Wien (europe 23) is the same tier of trip.
bucketList.whyAssistant: The country's biggest match, between its two most successful clubs, played at the Letná Stadium and the Stadion Eden.

bucketList.title: AFC Asian Cup 2027 (Saudi Arabia)
bucketList.why: 24 teams in Asia's national-team championship. Dates unverified.

bucketList.title: Africa Cup of Nations 2027 (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda)
bucketList.why: The first AFCON with three co-hosts, and the first in East Africa (the CECAFA region) since Ethiopia hosted in 1976, with 24 teams. Dates unverified.

bucketList.title: UEFA Nations League Finals 2027
bucketList.why: Four national teams play semi-finals, a third-place match and a final in one host country, from 9 to 13 June 2027. The host is not fixed yet: UEFA designates a pair of League A quarter-finalists, and the winner of that tie hosts.

bucketList.title: Men's Olympic football 2028 (Los Angeles)
bucketList.why: Under-23 tournament with up to three older players per squad and 12 men's teams, in seven stadiums in Los Angeles and six other US cities; the semi-finals and medal matches are at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.

bucketList.title: UEFA Euro 2028 (UK and Ireland)
bucketList.why: 24 teams in nine stadiums across England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland, with the final at Wembley. Casement Park in Belfast has had construction problems.

bucketList.title: FIFA World Cup 2030
bucketList.why: 48 teams in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with one centenary match each in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay, so matches on three continents. Final venue unconfirmed.

bucketList.title: UEFA Euro 2032 (Italy and Turkey)
bucketList.why: Matches in Italian and Turkish stadiums, awarded in October 2023.

bucketList.title: UEFA Champions League final
bucketList.why: One match in late May or early June at a neutral venue set years ahead. The finalists get most tickets, with a small public allocation (route unverified).

bucketList.title: UEFA Conference League final
bucketList.why: One match at a neutral venue, with a loud travelling crowd. The 2027 final is on 2 June 2027 at Beşiktaş Stadium in Istanbul, so not in May.

bucketList.title: UEFA Super Cup
bucketList.why: Champions League winner against Europa League winner in August at a rotating venue. Easier to get into than the finals.

bucketList.title: Copa Libertadores final
bucketList.why: One match with the venue chosen each year, South America's top club final, with an ultras atmosphere.

bucketList.title: MLS Cup
bucketList.why: Hosted by the finalist with the better regular-season record, so far in November or December; the league moves to a summer-to-spring schedule beginning in 2027, so the timing of the final changes. A US stadium and fan culture.

bucketList.title: DFB-Pokal final
bucketList.why: Played at the Olympiastadion Berlin each year, with both fan groups travelling. Underdogs reach it: third-division Bielefeld played VfB in 2025.

bucketList.title: Franz Beckenbauer Supercup
bucketList.why: Bundesliga champion against DFB-Pokal winner before the season, an early look at the top two German teams. Host stadium varies.

bucketList.title: Cupa României final
bucketList.why: The national cup decider. The venue is set in advance, normally in Bucharest.

bucketList.title: EFL Cup final
bucketList.why: Wembley in February or March, the first major trophy of the English season.

bucketList.title: FA Cup final
bucketList.why: Wembley in May, with a deep ritual around the day and fans of both finalists filling the stadium.

bucketList.title: FA Community Shield
bucketList.why: League champions against FA Cup winners in August, the season's curtain-raiser, normally at Wembley (the 2026 match was played in Cardiff).

bucketList.title: Coupe de France final
bucketList.why: Stade de France in May. Amateur clubs can reach it.

bucketList.title: Coppa Italia final
bucketList.why: Usually the Stadio Olimpico in Rome, with an Italian ultras final in the city's biggest stadium.

bucketList.title: KNVB Beker final
bucketList.why: Usually at De Kuip in Rotterdam. Feyenoord dropped their plans to leave it for a new stadium in 2022.

bucketList.title: Taça de Portugal final
bucketList.why: Estádio Nacional in Jamor, a fixed national occasion at a traditional ground with a day-out feel.

bucketList.title: Scottish Cup final
bucketList.why: Hampden Park in May, one of Europe's oldest big stadiums.

bucketList.title: Copa del Rey final
bucketList.why: One match in spring at La Cartuja in Seville, the regular venue since 2020, often with Barcelona or a Madrid club against a Basque or other regional crowd.

bucketList.title: Supercopa de España
bucketList.why: A four-team knockout since 2020, played in Saudi Arabia under an agreement that runs until at least 2029; the 2021 edition was held in Spain. Barcelona and Real Madrid met in each of the last four finals. The 2027 edition is to be moved to Istanbul because Saudi Arabia hosts the 2027 Asian Cup.

bucketList.title: Germany v Netherlands
bucketList.why: A long-running rivalry between two of Europe's football cultures. Scheduling varies.

bucketList.title: Romania national team home match
bucketList.why: Matches at the Arena Națională, the national stadium in Bucharest.

bucketList.title: Brazil v Argentina
bucketList.why: The South American derby, also called the Superderby of the Americas. They met in qualifiers for the 2002, 2006, 2010, 2018, 2022 and 2026 World Cups; the venue changes (since 2000 the Morumbi, the Mineirão and the Maracanã in Brazil, the Monumental, Rosario and San Juan in Argentina).

bucketList.title: England v Scotland
bucketList.why: The oldest international rivalry. No regular fixture exists now, so check what is scheduled.

bucketList.title: Arminia Bielefeld v Paderborn
bucketList.why: East Westphalia derby between two mid-sized clubs, with large fan groups on both sides.

bucketList.title: Bochum v Schalke
bucketList.why: Ruhr derby in a compact, football-only ground of about 26,000.

bucketList.title: Carl Zeiss Jena v Rot-Weiß Erfurt
bucketList.why: Thuringia derby between the state's two biggest clubs, from its two biggest cities. Jena's Ernst-Abbe-Sportfeld was rebuilt as a new stadium that opened in 2024; Erfurt's Steigerwaldstadion was rebuilt in 2015-2017.

bucketList.title: Dynamo Dresden v Erzgebirge Aue
bucketList.why: Saxony derby with one of Germany's best atmospheres in Dresden and a travelling Aue following.

bucketList.title: Eintracht Frankfurt v Darmstadt 98
bucketList.why: Hesse derby pairing a large modern stadium with the Böllenfalltor, which still has large standing terraces.

bucketList.title: Eintracht Frankfurt v Kickers Offenbach
bucketList.why: Main derby between neighbouring cities, played at the traditional, hostile Bieberer Berg when Offenbach host. Likely cup only.

bucketList.title: Eintracht Frankfurt v Mainz (Rhein-Main-Derby)
bucketList.why: Called the Rhein-Main-Derby in media reports, though Frankfurt's supporters do not regard it as a derby. Loud atmosphere in both stadiums.

bucketList.title: Hannover 96 v Eintracht Braunschweig
bucketList.why: Lower Saxony's main rivalry, with loyal away followings.

bucketList.title: Holstein Kiel v Hansa Rostock
bucketList.why: Two clubs from cities on the Baltic Sea, with Rostock's Ostseestadion among the loudest grounds in the east.

bucketList.title: Holstein Kiel v HSV
bucketList.why: North German meeting at Kiel's small Holstein-Stadion (15,034 places) on the Baltic; the two clubs shared every north German title from 1921 to 1933. HSV are in the Bundesliga and Kiel in the 2. Bundesliga in 2026/27, so likely cup only.

bucketList.title: HSV v St. Pauli (Hamburg derby)
bucketList.why: Two city clubs with opposite cultures, at the Volksparkstadion and the Millerntor, one of Germany's most distinctive grounds.

bucketList.title: Karlsruher SC v Freiburg
bucketList.why: Often called the Badisches Derby (Baden derby), between two stadiums of similar size (33,180 and 34,700 places), about 119 km apart in a straight line.

bucketList.title: FC Köln v Bayer Leverkusen
bucketList.why: Rhineland derby between Köln's loud, city-wide support and Leverkusen's compact ground.

bucketList.title: FC Köln v Borussia Mönchengladbach
bucketList.why: Long, bitter Rhineland rivalry with strong atmospheres at both grounds.

bucketList.title: FC Köln v Fortuna Düsseldorf (Rheinderby)
bucketList.why: Two cities about 40 km apart with a long rivalry.

bucketList.title: FC Magdeburg v Hallescher FC
bucketList.why: Saxony-Anhalt derby, with a loud, big home stand in Magdeburg and a strong Halle following.

bucketList.title: Lok Leipzig v Chemie Leipzig
bucketList.why: Leipzig city derby in the Regionalliga, with large fan groups, choreography and old grounds that put the crowd at the pitch.

bucketList.title: Preußen Münster v VfL Osnabrück
bucketList.why: Westphalia-Lower Saxony derby between two grounds with standing terraces.

bucketList.title: Rot-Weiss Essen v MSV Duisburg
bucketList.why: Ruhr derby with working-class grounds and a strong ultra presence.

bucketList.title: Saarbrücken v SV Elversberg
bucketList.why: Two Saarland clubs about 13 km apart in a straight line: 1. FC Saarbrücken, a founding member of the Bundesliga in 1963, and SV Elversberg, who rose from the fourth tier in 2022 to the Bundesliga in 2026, at small grounds (Ludwigspark 16,003 places, Waldstadion Kaiserlinde 10,000).

bucketList.title: Union Berlin v Hertha BSC (Berlin derby)
bucketList.why: East against west: Union's mostly standing Alte Försterei against Hertha's Olympiastadion.

bucketList.title: Union Berlin Weihnachtssingen
bucketList.why: Christmas carol event, held since 2003, where fans fill the pitch and terraces of the Alte Försterei. Not a match.

bucketList.title: VfB Stuttgart v Freiburg
bucketList.why: Baden-Württemberg Bundesliga fixture, with VfB's Cannstatter Kurve against Freiburg's modern stadium.

bucketList.title: VfB Stuttgart v Stuttgarter Kickers
bucketList.why: City derby played at the Gazi-Stadion auf der Waldau, a small, steep ground on a wooded hillside. Only possible through the cup.

bucketList.title: Waldhof Mannheim v 1. FC Kaiserslautern
bucketList.why: A rivalry that grew in the 1980s, also known as the Südwest-Derby and regarded as one of Germany's hottest derbies; the grounds are about 53 km apart in a straight line.

bucketList.title: Werder Bremen v HSV (Nordderby)
bucketList.why: Northern German classic, the Weserstadion against the Volksparkstadion.

bucketList.title: CFR Cluj v Universitatea Cluj
bucketList.why: Cluj derby, a city split into two clubs.

bucketList.title: Rapid București v Dinamo București
bucketList.why: The other Bucharest derby, with Rapid's Giulești as a compact, modern ground (opened 2022, 14,047 seats).

bucketList.title: 2. Bundesliga relegation play-off against the 3. Liga

trigger.playedMonthStatus: inferred - observed in the 2026 play-off only (22 and 26 May)

bucketList.whyAssistant: Two-legged tie between the 16th-placed 2. Bundesliga club and the 3rd-placed 3. Liga club, decided on aggregate with no away-goals rule, then extra time and penalties. The winner plays in the 2. Bundesliga next season, the loser in the 3. Liga. In 2026 the third-tier club hosted the first leg - the DFB gives the return leg at home to the club with fewer free days before the first leg; Essen won it 1:0 and Fürth won the return 2:0 at home to stay up. The participants are unknown until the last matchday.

bucketList.title: Aufstiegsspiele zur 3. Liga (Regionalliga champions' play-off)
bucketList.whyAssistant: Not a 3. Liga club against a Regionalliga club: two Regionalliga champions play home and away for the last promotion place to the 3. Liga, while the other promotion places go to champions directly. The sources describe the model as two direct places (West, Südwest), one rotating direct place for Nord, Nordost or Bayern, and a two-legged play-off between the other two champions; in 2025/26 the direct places went to Südwest, West and Nord. In the vote at the end of June 2026 no reform model found a majority. The DFB is preparing an extraordinary Bundestag on 18 December 2026 on a model with four instead of five Regionalligen, which would start in 2028/29 with 2027/28 as a qualifying season, so the current model is expected to apply in 2026/27 - not confirmed by a DFB statement. Which two clubs meet is unknown until the Regionalliga seasons end. In 2026 Würzburger Kickers beat Nordost champions Lok Leipzig in this play-off, 1:0 and 2:1; Würzburg took part as runners-up of the Regionalliga Bayern because the champions, 1. FC Nürnberg II, did not take a 3. Liga licence.

bucketList.title: Superliga relegation play-off against Liga 2

trigger.playedMonthStatus: inferred - observed in the 2025-26 play-offs only (first legs around 23 May, return legs up to 1 June)

bucketList.whyAssistant: In 2025-26 the two Superliga clubs just above the directly relegated 15th and 16th places each met one of the top Liga 2 clubs (the third and fourth placed) in a two-legged tie. In 2026 Farul Constanța drew 3-3 and 1-1 with Chindia Târgoviște and stayed up on penalties; FC Voluntari lost 2-3 at Hermannstadt, then won 3-0 at home and went up. Which clubs meet is unknown until the end of the play-out. The 2026-27 competition rules were not found, so the format may change.

bucketList.title: Liga 3 promotion tournament for the last Liga 2 place

trigger.playedMonthStatus: inferred - observed in the 2025-26 cycle only (final scheduled for 6 June 2026)

bucketList.whyAssistant: Not a match between Liga 2 and Liga 3 clubs: the runners-up of the four Liga 3 play-off groups play single-match semi-finals and a final, with the first semi-final's winner hosting the final, and the winner takes the fifth promotion place to Liga 2. The group winners go up directly. The 2025-26 rules are from the federation's competition system and press; the 2026-27 rules were not found.
